plan.title: Heart RNA-seq: genotype x drug interaction analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question — does the drug act differently in KO vs WT — is formally a genotype x treatment interaction question in a 2x2 factorial bulk RNA-seq design (WT/KO x vehicle/drug, n=4/cell, 16 samples, 12000 genes, raw Salmon counts, heart, Homo sapiens). Testing this correctly requires a single DESeq2-style negative-binomial GLM fit with a full factorial design (~genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment) rather than four separate pairwise contrasts, because only the interaction (genotype:treatment) coefficient directly tests whether the treatment effect differs by genotype; running simple contrasts risks the classic error of concluding 'different' from one being significant and the other not without ever testing the difference-of-differences. Per the user's explicit constraint, PyDESeq2 (Python, present in the sandbox, published and validated against DESeq2) is used instead of R's DESeq2. The plan proceeds: (1) QC/normalization and exploratory structure (PCA/library size) on the 12000x16 count matrix to confirm the four experimental groups separate and to catch outlier samples before model fitting; (2) fit the full interaction model and extract three coefficients — the main effect of genotype in vehicle, the main effect of drug in WT, and the interaction term itself, which is the direct answer to the research question; (3) for genes with a significant interaction, also report the drug-vs-vehicle simple effect within each genotype stratum (WT-only and KO-only contrasts, obtained either via re-leveling or via the interaction model directly) so the direction and magnitude of genotype-dependent drug response is interpretable, not just its existence; (4) pathway enrichment on the interaction-significant gene set using WikiPathways/Reactome/MSigDB human gene sets (all present in the reference store) to give the interaction result biological interpretation; (5) an interaction-gene PPI submodule analysis using the STRING human network to check whether interaction genes cluster on the interactome (supports a coherent genotype-dependent mechanism versus a scattered/noisy signal). No translational/PK/safety steps are added because the research question is a pure genotype x treatment mechanistic question with no compound identity, dose-response, clinical outcome, or safety data given — adding those would be speculative.
